blurb: Real analysis from the completeness of ℝ to the Lebesgue integral, with multivariable calculus and full proofs.

pics.alt: Graph of a Weierstrass function between x = −2 and x = 2, jagged at every scale, with a circular zoomed inset
pics.caption: A Weierstrass function on [−2, 2], with an inset magnifying a small piece of the graph near the red point. Functions of this kind, presented by Weierstrass in 1872, are continuous everywhere but differentiable nowhere.
pics.title: WeierstrassFunction.svg

pics.alt: Black-and-white portrait of Bernhard Riemann, bearded and wearing spectacles and a bow tie
pics.caption: Bernhard Riemann (1826–1866), in a portrait from 1863. His 1854 Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series introduced the integral that bears his name.
pics.title: Georg Friedrich Bernhard Riemann.jpeg
